request.system: You are a precise classification engine. You reply with a code and nothing else: no explanation, no punctuation, no preamble.

messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode of care described below. A three-character category is one capital letter followed by exactly two digits, for example J44.

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY:

Admission Date: N/A
Discharge Date: N/A

Patient: 63-year-old woman
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course Summary: 

The patient underwent an excision of a vulvar lesion and it was diagnosed as a BG-ACC. Although the patient did not undergo adjuvant therapy, the diagnosis was followed up. However, 4 years later, the patient was found to have metastasis to the lung. A video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery was performed which was followed by recurrence in the vulva 5 years later. The patient subsequently underwent an excision of the recurrent vulvar lesion which was used for molecular analysis.

The patient's case exempts her from being discharged or having any medication prescriptions. Further re-examinations may be conducted in the following weeks. 

Follow-up Care: The patient is advised to return for follow-up re-examinations as required by the treating physician.

Signed,
[Name and Title of Physician]

Reply with the three characters only.

text:
BG-ACC is Bartholin gland adenoid cystic carcinoma. In ICD-10, a Bartholin gland malignancy is coded under vulva (C51), with Bartholin gland included under C51.0 labia majora or C51.9 vulva unspecified. The episode involves a recurrent vulvar lesion excision, so C51 is the principal category, even though lung metastasis is also present.

C51
